key: A housing society secretary in Chennai
name: ch02_society_fine_vs_board
alt: A split picture of a Chennai apartment block: on the left a watchman stands over waste bins next to a fine notice, on the right residents happily sort waste beside a lift notice board where their floor's name is up.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves set in the ground-floor lobby of the same Chennai apartment block with a lift door and pale yellow walls. LEFT panel: a stern middle-aged watchman (khaki uniform, cap, moustache, wooden stick under his arm) stands with arms folded beside two bins, one green and one blue; a printed notice on the wall shows a big red cross and "500". A resident in a nightie and dupatta drops a bag in the right bin while glancing nervously at the watchman; a dotted line behind her shows that once the watchman walks away, the next bag goes into the wrong bin. A large label "FINE" sits at the top of the left panel. RIGHT panel: no watchman. A cork notice board beside the lift shows a gold star and the words "FLOOR 3". Two children (about 9 and 11, shorts and T-shirts) proudly carry neatly sorted bags to the green and blue bins, while a grandmother in a cotton sari watches smiling, holding a small paper diya to hint at the Diwali event the floor gets to pick. Small upward arrows rise from the children toward the board. A large label "PRIDE" sits at the top of the right panel. Bright morning light, gentle and cheerful mood: one rule needs a guard, the other runs itself.

key: A joint family in Lucknow: everyone gets
name: ch02_daughter_in_law_unseen
alt: A Lucknow joint family eats a full meal at a long table while the daughter-in-law who cooked it stands at the side holding the ladle, unnoticed, with an empty speech bubble above her.
scene: A wide interior view of a joint-family dining room in an old Lucknow house, arched window, ceiling fan, a long low table covered with steel thalis full of dal, rotis and rice. Around the table from left to right: a grandfather in a white kurta and Nehru cap eating with his head down, a middle-aged man in a shirt scrolling his phone while chewing, and two school children in uniform with school bags propped against their chairs, all clearly fed and comfortable. On the right side, standing slightly apart near the kitchen doorway, the daughter-in-law (about 32, green cotton sari with the pallu tucked at the waist, hair in a bun) holds a steel ladle and a pot of dal, looking at the family with a hopeful, tired face. Nobody looks at her. Above the table a small row of ticks shows meals, bed and school fees covered. Above her head floats a large speech bubble that is completely empty, with a faint dotted outline, showing the words of thanks nobody says. A large label "FED" floats above the table on the left, and a large label "UNSEEN" sits above the daughter-in-law on the right. Warm evening lamp light, quiet and slightly sad mood: the bodies are fed, her need to matter is not.

key: A grandfather in a Punjab village keeps
name: ch02_buffalo_certificates_wall
alt: A proud Punjabi grandfather points visiting relatives to a wall of framed cattle-fair certificates while, through the window, his buffaloes chew in the shed, uninterested.
scene: A cosy front room of a village house in Punjab with whitewashed walls, a charpai, a steel trunk and a tall window on the right. On the left wall hang six framed certificates in two rows, each with a small rosette ribbon, and one frame showing a simple drawing of a buffalo with a gold medal. In front of the wall, the grandfather (about 75, white kurta-pyjama, bright orange turban, white beard, walking stick) points proudly at the frames with his free hand, chest out and beaming. Beside him stand two visiting relatives from abroad: a man in his 40s in a puffer jacket and jeans holding a roller suitcase handle, and his teenage daughter in a hoodie, both smiling politely and leaning in to look. Through the window on the right we see the cattle shed outside: two big black buffaloes chewing hay, heads down, entirely uninterested, one with its tail flicking. A thin dashed arrow links the frames to the grandfather's heart to show where the pride lives. A large label "PRIDE" sits above the certificate wall. Soft winter afternoon light through the window, warm and affectionate, gently funny mood: the animals earned the prize, the man feels it.

key: Three cousins in Kochi, all hungry to be
name: ch02_three_cousins_outlets
alt: Three cousins in Kochi feed the same hunger to be noticed in three ways: one holds up an exam result to clapping neighbours, one poses by an oversized SUV with an EMI bill, one watches a view counter climb as a police jeep arrives.
scene: A three-panel illustration in a row, separated by thin vertical lines, set on the same coconut-palm-lined lane in Kochi with tiled-roof houses. Over all three panels runs a faint dotted line joining a small empty bowl icon above each cousin's head, showing the same hunger. LEFT panel: a slim 18-year-old in a white shirt and mundu holds up a printed result sheet with a big tick, while two neighbours, an aunty at her gate and an old man on a bicycle, clap. Label "WORK" at the top. MIDDLE panel: a young man in sunglasses and a shiny shirt leans against a huge dark SUV that barely fits the narrow lane; a long paper bill unrolls from his pocket to the ground with a red "EMI" stamp, and a small sweat drop on his forehead. Label "SHOW" at the top. RIGHT panel: a third cousin with a torn T-shirt sleeve and a bruise grins at his phone, whose screen shows a rising arrow and "1M"; behind him a police jeep with a blue light pulls up and a constable steps out. Label "TROUBLE" at the top. Bright tropical daylight, lively mood: one hunger, three very different meals.

key: Two well-known men in a small town in
name: ch02_eye_camp_vs_strongman
alt: In a small Bihar town, one man is greeted with folded hands at his free eye camp while another strongman walks the market and shopkeepers shrink in fear; both wear the same thought bubble showing the town knowing their name.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves on the same dusty market street of a small town in Bihar with shop shutters and a tea stall. LEFT panel: a canopy tent with a white banner showing a simple eye symbol; an elderly woman in a sari has her eyes checked by a doctor with a torch, and in the front a plump middle-aged man in a cream kurta and shawl stands smiling while two villagers greet him with folded hands. Label "RESPECT" at the top. RIGHT panel: a tall burly man in a white safari suit, gold chain and dark glasses walks past shops flanked by one henchman; a vegetable seller cowers behind his cart and a cloth merchant quickly lowers his eyes, a small "!" badge floating above them. Label "FEAR" at the top. Above both main men float identical thought bubbles, each showing a tiny town with many small faces turned toward a single figure, making it clear the hidden wish is the same: to be known. Winter morning light with long shadows; warm on the left, slightly cold and tense on the right. The two halves mirror each other in composition so the viewer compares the outlets, not the men.

key: A retired IAS officer in Delhi still has
name: ch02_names_on_everything
alt: A retired officer stands proudly by his gate nameplate, while behind him a stadium stand and a college arch carry giant names, showing that the wish to be remembered never switches off.
scene: A wide street-level view of a leafy Delhi colony at morning. In the FOREGROUND LEFT, a retired officer (about 80, white hair, spectacles, grey safari suit, walking stick) stands beside his gate pillar, chin up, admiring a polished brass nameplate that reads "IAS (RETD.)"; his phone in one hand shows the same title on a profile screen, and a stack of visiting cards peeks from his pocket. In the MIDDLE, through the trees, rises a cricket stadium stand with a huge blank banner across it and a tiny figure of a retired cricketer in a blazer pointing up at it. On the RIGHT, a new college hall with a tall arch carries a band of enormous blocky letters across the top (shown as thick abstract bars, not readable words), and a businessman in a suit and his old father stand below, looking up with satisfaction while a mason on a ladder fixes the last letter. Dashed lines link all three names back to a single glowing spark above the old officer's head, showing the same urge in each. A large label "MY NAME" sits centred at the top. Clear morning sun, gently humorous mood: each man has achieved plenty, and still wants his name seen.

key: A retired grandfather in Kolkata, whose
name: ch02_grandfather_bp_calls
alt: A split picture of a Kolkata grandfather: well and alone on his balcony with a silent phone on the left; unwell with a blood pressure cuff on the right while his phone rings nonstop with calls from his children.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same retired grandfather (about 72, white dhoti and cream kurta, spectacles, thinning grey hair) in both halves inside his old Kolkata flat with green shutters and a tall wooden almirah. LEFT panel: he sits upright and healthy in a cane chair on the balcony reading a newspaper, a cup of tea steaming beside him and a potted tulsi plant; his old phone lies on a stool, its screen dark, with a small hourglass floating above it and a tiny calendar showing days passing. Label "FINE" at the top. RIGHT panel: the same man lies on a bed propped on pillows with a blood pressure cuff on his arm and a strip of tablets on the bedside table; his phone buzzes with motion lines and three overlapping incoming-call bubbles show small faces of a son in an office shirt, a daughter with a laptop bag, and a grandchild waving, with tiny map pins for distant cities. A gentle half-smile on his tired face shows he feels both unwell and cared for. Label "UNWELL" at the top. Soft light on the left, warmer busy light on the right. The mechanism is plain: attention arrives only with illness.

key: Two cricket coaches at a Mumbai academy.
name: ch02_two_cricket_coaches
alt: Two cricket coaches at a Mumbai academy: one ignores a row of good shots and shouts at the single bad one; the other claps a good cover drive and keeps the fix for later.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves on the same green practice nets of a Mumbai cricket academy with a high net fence and a distant row of buildings. In each half a teenage batsman (about 15, white kit, helmet, pads) plays a shot. LEFT panel: above the batsman a row of small green ticks shows many good shots, all faded and ignored, followed by one red cross; the coach (stocky, 50s, tracksuit, cap, whistle) stands far off with hands cupped around his mouth, shouting, a jagged speech bubble with only "!" in it. The boy's shoulders slump and his bat points down. Label "FAULTS" at the top. RIGHT panel: the row of ticks is bright and each one has a small star; the second coach (lean, 40s, academy polo shirt, clipboard under his arm) claps with a warm smile, a speech bubble with a cricket bat and a sparkle. A small inset in the corner shows the same coach later, sitting with the boy on a bench, pointing quietly at a little diagram of a pull shot. The boy stands tall, grinning. Label "PRAISE" at the top. Bright afternoon light; the left side feels tense, the right side relaxed and keen.

key: A textile trader in Surat sends his
name: ch02_surat_nephew_loss
alt: In a Surat cotton trading shop, an older uncle rests a reassuring hand on his worried nephew's shoulder beside a falling price chart, instead of shouting at him.
scene: An interior view of a traditional textile trading office in Surat: white mattress seating on the floor with bolsters, a low wooden desk with a ledger and calculator, cotton bales stacked on the right with burlap wrapping and rope. On the wall behind hangs a simple price board showing a line chart that falls steeply, with a red downward arrow and the label "LOSS" beside it. In the centre, the nephew (about 26, checked shirt, a small travel bag still on his shoulder) stands with his head bowed and hands clasped, braced for a scolding; a small cloud of dread with lightning hovers over his head, but it is dissolving. The uncle (about 60, white kurta, Nehru jacket, spectacles pushed up on his forehead) has risen from the gaddi and places one hand gently on the nephew's shoulder, the other hand open in an easy, forgiving gesture, with a calm, kind smile. A dashed arrow from the uncle's hand leads to a small inset bubble on the right showing the same nephew months later, carefully checking a cotton sample with a magnifying glass. A large label "TRUST" sits at the top centre. Warm late-afternoon light through a shuttered window, calm and steady mood.

key: In many Indian homes the mother has
name: ch02_tiffin_only_pickle
alt: A split picture: on the left a family silently takes the same full tiffin for years; on the right the mother packs only pickle and the whole family suddenly crowds around talking.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in the same small Indian kitchen with a gas stove, a steel shelf and a wall calendar. The mother (about 50, cotton printed sari, bindi, hair tied back) stands at the counter in both. LEFT panel: an open three-tier steel tiffin box shows two rotis, sabzi and a little pickle; a stack of many identical closed tiffins behind it suggests years of the same routine, and the calendar's pages fly away. A husband in an office shirt and a college-going son with earphones grab their tiffins without looking up, mouths closed, no speech bubbles at all. Label "25 YEARS" at the top. RIGHT panel: the open tiffin holds only a small heap of red mango pickle in each tier. The husband, the son and a daughter in a school uniform crowd around the counter, wide-eyed, three speech bubbles popping out of them filled with "?" and "!" marks. The mother stands with arms folded and a quiet, knowing face. Label "ONE DAY" at the top. Morning light; flat and grey on the left, bright and noisy on the right, showing that people only speak up when the care stops.

key: A Gujarati household where the grandmother
name: ch02_thepla_but_no_praise
alt: In a Gujarati home, the grandmother lovingly packs thepla for every guest while, beside her, the son holding his college topper certificate hears only a question about his next exam.
scene: A wide interior view of a Gujarati family home with a swing (hichko) in the living room, a carved wooden door and a framed family photo. On the LEFT, the grandmother (about 75, white-bordered sari worn Gujarati style, spectacles) presses a large steel box of thepla into the hands of a visiting cousin carrying a backpack, with two more boxes waiting on the table; little hearts float up from the food. Above her a large label "FED". On the RIGHT, the son (about 22, light blue shirt) holds up a framed certificate with a gold seal and a big ribbon, eyes bright and hopeful. Facing him, his father (about 52, half-sleeve shirt, reading glasses, newspaper folded under his arm) raises one eyebrow; his speech bubble contains only the short text "GATE?" The son's hopeful arrow toward the father is drooping. Above the son a large label "STARVED" with a small empty plate icon. A dashed arrow from the son to the food on the left shows the irony: plenty for the body, nothing for self-esteem. Warm afternoon light through the window, affectionate but bittersweet mood.

key: A quiet Class 6 student in a government
name: ch02_quiet_boy_fixes_speaker
alt: A Madurai teacher hands a silent speaker to a quiet schoolboy before assembly; he fixes it while classmates watch, and an inset shows him grown up in his own sound studio.
scene: A wide view of an open courtyard of a government school in Madurai, a yellow building with blue window grills, a neem tree and rows of students in white shirts and navy shorts or pinafores lined up for assembly. On a small stage at the LEFT stands a projector screen and a box loudspeaker with a red cross over its sound waves. In the CENTRE, a kind woman teacher (about 40, cotton sari, jasmine in her hair, spectacles) kneels to the level of a thin, quiet Class 6 boy (oiled hair, oversized uniform shirt) and hands him a small screwdriver, her other hand gesturing at the speaker. The boy looks up surprised, a faint glow around him showing he has been seen. Beside him the speaker's back panel is open and its sound waves are now green and flowing out toward the students, who turn and look with interest. A large label "SEEN" sits above the boy and teacher. On the RIGHT, a round inset bubble joined by a dashed line shows the same boy as a grown man in his 30s at a mixing desk in a recording studio with headphones round his neck, smiling as he tells a story. Small text "20 YEARS" on the dashed line. Bright morning light, hopeful mood.

key: Every Indian office knows the chamcha
name: ch02_chamcha_vs_sincere
alt: A split office picture: a bowing flatterer heaps vague praise on a boss who rolls his eyes, while a colleague's specific, quiet compliment makes the same boss smile.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, both halves in the same open-plan Indian office with cubicle partitions, a whiteboard and a water cooler. The boss (about 50, blue shirt, red tie, slight paunch) sits at his desk in both halves. LEFT panel: an eager employee (about 35, oiled hair, too-tight shirt) bends low beside the boss holding out a flower garland and a box of sweets; a big frilly speech bubble overflows with hearts, stars and thumbs-up icons, aimed at the boss's tie. A tiny ladder with the word "PROMOTION" leans against the wall behind him. The boss rolls his eyes toward the viewer and two colleagues in the background smirk. Label "FLATTERY" at the top. RIGHT panel: a colleague (about 30, kurta and lanyard, holding a laptop) stands upright at the doorway; her small, plain speech bubble shows a tiny drawing of a complaint letter turning into a roadmap arrow, a specific thing the boss did. The boss leans back, genuinely smiling, one hand on his chest. Label "SINCERE" at the top. Bright office lighting; the left feels sticky and fake, the right calm and real.

key: A regular at a Bengaluru darshini tells
name: ch02_darshini_dosa_friend
alt: At a busy Bengaluru darshini, a regular customer compliments the dosa cook over the counter; the cook beams, waves and slides his plate out first with extra chutney.
scene: A street-front view of a standing-only Bengaluru darshini: steel counter, a wide black tawa with three dosas spreading, steam rising, a menu board of plain icons, stainless steel tumblers of filter coffee lined up. Behind the tawa, the cook (about 45, white vest, towel over his shoulder, headband, moustache) beams and raises his spatula in a friendly wave. In front of the counter, the regular customer (about 30, office lanyard, backpack, rolled-up sleeves) gives a thumbs-up, a speech bubble with a small crisp dosa and a sparkle. Between them, a plate slides across the counter with a golden folded masala dosa and three small bowls of chutney instead of two, a tiny "+1" near the extra bowl. Behind the customer, two other customers still wait with token slips, one checking his watch, to show his plate came first. Along the bottom edge a thin strip shows a row of five small calendar squares each marked "FRI" with a little heart growing bigger along the row. A large label "FRIENDS" at the top centre. Bright, busy morning light with steam and warmth; cheerful, small-moment mood.

key: In a school hostel in Dehradun, the mess
name: ch02_hostel_poha_praise
alt: In a Dehradun school hostel mess, the warden stands and publicly praises the shy mess helper's poha while rows of boys at long tables clap.
scene: A wide interior view of a school hostel dining hall in Dehradun: long wooden tables with steel plates, high windows showing pine-covered hills, and a serving counter with big steel pots on the right. Behind the counter, the mess helper (about 40, white apron, cap, thin moustache) holds a large ladle over a pot of yellow poha with green chillies and peanuts, looking up startled, a faint blush. A small faded inset bubble behind his head shows a burnt roti with a crossed-out laughing face, the old jokes now fading. In the CENTRE-LEFT, the warden (about 55, tweed jacket, spectacles, grey hair) stands at the head of a table with one arm extended toward the helper, speaking loudly, a speech bubble containing a steaming plate of poha and a star. At the tables, four or five boys in grey sweaters and school ties turn toward the counter and clap, with more rows fading into the background to imply a hundred. A large label "PRAISE" sits above the warden. A dashed arrow from the warden's hand runs to the helper. Crisp morning light through the windows, warm and uplifting mood.

key: On a long train journey from Delhi to
name: ch02_train_thank_you
alt: Inside a sleeper coach, a traveller thanks the auntie sharing lemon rice, a student who lifted his bag, and the ticket examiner who sorted his berth, as fields rush past the window.
scene: A cut-away interior view of an Indian railway sleeper coach compartment: blue berths stacked in three tiers, a barred window on the right with green fields and a palm tree streaking past, a steel chain and a water bottle hanging. In the CENTRE, the traveller (about 30, T-shirt, track pants, backpack at his feet) sits on the lower berth with palms pressed together in a warm namaste, smiling. On the LEFT, a cheerful auntie (about 55, silk-cotton sari, big bindi, spectacles) holds out an open steel box of yellow lemon rice with a spoon, and a small speech bubble with a heart floats between them. Behind the traveller, a college student (about 20, hoodie, earphones round his neck) reaches up to set the traveller's suitcase on the top luggage rack. On the RIGHT, the ticket examiner (about 50, black coat, white shirt, clipboard of berth charts) gives a small nod, pointing to a berth number. Small green ticks appear next to each of the three helpers. At the bottom edge, a thin dashed track line runs off toward the right with a small sign showing a far-away station, hinting the journey ends and they will never meet again. A large label "ONCE" at the top centre. Golden afternoon light from the window, gentle, grateful mood.
